title: Frame
direction: Evolve the crop-mark idea: a selection frame whose open corners form a lowercase m
rationale: A crop frame says 'this is the part that counts'; opened at the right corners it reads as an m. Evolution of the existing equity, not a copy.

sketchReview.notes: Keep: two corner brackets facing each other become the m arches, bracket idea carries the letter. Fix: red stem is a tiny tick, enlarge or drop it; the arch silhouette is tunnel/magnet-like, sharpen shoulders (crop-mark squareness vs full round) to own it; avoid s3 which reads as ITI.

brand-fit.rationale: Evolves the crop-mark heritage into something precise; calm, technical, fits the tone

semantic-relevance.rationale: i-in-m is clever on paper but the idea needs explaining; frame-as-crop still ties to the product

distinctiveness.rationale: Bracket pair plus stem is more ownable than the generic focus glyph, but still near crop/viewfinder UI icons

memorability.rationale: Reads as ri/rit or an 'rh' first; no single gesture sticks, m recognition needs a hint

balance.rationale: Symmetric and calm; top-heavy open bottom feels slightly unsupported

craft.rationale: Clean but the 1 px stem at 16 px and amber dot gap are fragile; brackets are plain rectangles

typography.rationale: Grotesk wordmark with amber square i-dot echoes the symbol sensibly

color.rationale: Amber #c07000 is clearly away from coral but dull ochre-brown; delta 17.7 only moderate

timelessness.rationale: Geometric, but bracket-glyph feels like UI trend

versatility.rationale: Mono works; 16 px tiny and loses the m reading
